mainTopic: Action in עדים זוממין, and the forbidden practices of בעל אוב, ידעוני, דורש אל המתים, מעונן and מנחש
overview: The amud opens with רבי זירא challenging רבא: a ברייתא says עדים זוממין bring no קרבן חטאת because their sin has no action, even though they actually spoke. רבא first answers that their sin is only through the voice (קול). The גמרא shows this does not fit רבי יוחנן, who holds that moving the mouth (עקימת פיו) is an action. So רבא answers instead that their testimony rests on sight (ראייה). The גמרא then defines a בעל אוב and a ידעוני and defends the definition against two פסוקים. A second ברייתא describes two kinds of בעל אוב, one of which does not work on שבת. That leads to the story of טורנוסרופוס asking רבי עקיבא what makes שבת special. The גמרא explains דורש אל המתים, which brings רבי עקיבא's tears and רבא's teaching that צדיקים could create a world, backed by two stories of creation. The amud ends with ברייתות defining a מעונן and a מנחש.

steps.title: רבי זירא challenges רבא using conspiring witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא quotes a ברייתא that עדים זוממין are left out of bringing a קרבן חטאת because their sin has no action. He asks why, since their sin is spoken and is not just in the heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא objected: A ברייתא says that עדים זוממין are left out (of bringing a חטאת), because their sin has no action. But why? Their sin is not just in the heart! (They actually spoke.)
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא attacks רבא's idea that a sin done by speaking, and not just by thinking, counts as an action. He brings a ברייתא where witnesses who sin by speaking are said to have no action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא had treated a sin done with words, not only in the heart, as having a מעשה. False witnesses sin only with words, yet the ברייתא says their sin has no מעשה. So רבא's idea seems to be contradicted.

keyTerms.meaning: Conspiring false witnesses, shown to be lying because they were somewhere else at the time
A physical action
In the heart, meaning only in thought

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the ברייתא is saying עדים זוממין did nothing wrong. It only says they don't bring a קרבן חטאת, because a חטאת is brought only for a sin that involves an action.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira raises an objection:
Conspiring witnesses are excluded,
phrases.notes: This is from a ברייתא about who brings a קרבן חטאת. These witnesses don't bring one.

phrases.english: since there is no action in their sin.
But why?
Their sin is not just in the heart!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's earlier statement from before this section, that a spoken sin, which is not only in the heart, counts as an action.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's view that a sin done through speech, and not only in thought, counts as a מעשה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: עדים זוממין sin only through speech, yet the ברייתא says their sin has no מעשה. This contradicts the idea that speech is an action.

steps.title: רבא: witnesses are different because their sin is through the voice
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that עדים זוממין are a special case, because their sin is done through the voice (קול), and voice is not an action.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: עדים זוממין are different, since their sin is through the voice.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends himself by saying the witnesses are different from the case he was talking about. Their sin is done through the voice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא separates two things: moving the mouth to speak, and just making a sound heard. The witnesses' sin is about being heard in court, which is just 'voice'. A voice alone is not a physical action, so there is no קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different, a special case
Since, because
Voice, sound

phrases.english: Rava said:
Conspiring witnesses are different,
since their sin is through the voice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's challenge by showing that עדים זוממין are a special case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction (חילוק): voice is different from other speech
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any sin done through speech, and not just in the heart, counts as an action, so witnesses should bring a קרבן.
steps.terutzMaskana: Witnesses sin through their voice alone, and voice does not count as an action, so they bring no קרבן.

steps.title: But for רבי יוחנן, voice is an action
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבא's answer works for רבי יוחנן. It quotes a מחלוקת where someone muzzled an animal or led mixed animals using only his voice. רבי יוחנן says he is liable, so voice seems to count as an action.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is voice not an action according to רבי יוחנן? But it was said: If someone muzzled an animal with his voice, or led (mixed animals) with his voice, רבי יוחנן says he is liable, and ריש לקיש says he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's answer. It brings an argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש showing that רבי יוחנן treats using one's voice as an action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said voice is not an action. But רבי יוחנן holds a person is punished for muzzling or leading animals just by voice. That only makes sense if voice counts as a מעשה, so רבא's answer would not fit רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: He muzzled it, stopping the animal from eating while it works
He led it, making different kinds of animals work together
Liable, guilty
Exempt, not liable

phrases.english: And voice, according to Rabbi Yochanan,
is it not an action?
But wasn't it stated:
If one muzzled an animal with his voice
phrases.notes: דברים 25:4. He yelled at the animal every time it tried to eat.

phrases.english: or led animals together with his voice,
phrases.notes: דברים 22:10, not plowing with an ox and a donkey together.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says: He is liable,
and Reish Lakish says: He is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקוֹל, לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, לָאו מַעֲשֶׂה הוּא? וְהָא אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's answer from step 2 that voice is not an action.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that a sin done through voice has no מעשה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן holds one is liable for muzzling or leading animals by voice alone. That shows voice counts as an action for him, which goes against רבא's answer.

steps.title: The reasons: is moving the mouth an action?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the reasons in the מחלוקת. רבי יוחנן holds that moving the mouth counts as an action. ריש לקיש holds that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says he is liable, because moving the mouth is an action. ריש לקיש says he is exempt, because moving the mouth is not an action.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why each one ruled the way he did. This finishes the proof against רבא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole argument depends on one question: does moving your mouth to speak count as a physical action? רבי יוחנן says yes, which makes it clear that for him any sin done by voice involves a מעשה. That is the problem for רבא, and the next step gives his new answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Twisting or moving one's mouth to speak
Is, counts as

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן: moving the mouth (עקימת פיו) counts as an action. ריש לקיש: it does not. Because of this, רבא's answer about קול seems to work only for ריש לקיש. In the next step, רבא gives a new answer that fits רבי יוחנן too.
steps.whyThisMatters: The question of עקימת פיו decides whether sins done by speaking need a קרבן and whether one is punished with מלקות for them. This idea comes up in many places in ש"ס.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says he is liable,
because twisting his mouth counts as an action.
Reish Lakish says he is exempt,
because twisting his mouth does not count as an action.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: חַיָּיב, עֲקִימַת פִּיו הָוֵי מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the מחלוקת quoted in step 3, which completes the challenge to רבא.
steps.raayaObject: That according to רבי יוחנן, a sin done through voice counts as a מעשה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The reasoning of רבי יוחנן in the muzzling and leading case: moving the mouth (עקימת פיו) counts as an action

steps.title: רבא's new answer: witnesses depend on sight
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a new answer: עדים זוממין are different because their testimony depends on seeing, and seeing is not an action.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא says: עדים זוממין are different, because their testimony is based on sight.
steps.whatsHappening: Because of the challenge from רבי יוחנן, רבא drops his answer about קול. He gives a new reason why עדים זוממין do not bring a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answer, that voice is not an action, does not work for רבי יוחנן, who says moving the mouth counts as an action. So רבא moves the focus away from their speech and onto their seeing. The heart of their testimony is what they claim they saw, and seeing involves no action at all. That fits both רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the earlier answer is being dropped.
It is different. This is a special case.
Seeing. Here it means the eyewitness side of testimony.
Since, or because.

steps.whatToRemember: The final answer is that עדים זוממין have no action because their testimony rests on sight (ראייה), not because voice is not an action.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not the same answer as Step 2. רבא is replacing the קול answer with a new reason, because the קול answer clashes with רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava says:
Conspiring witnesses are different,
since they are [liable] through sight.
phrases.notes: Their testimony is about what they claim they saw, and seeing is not a physical action.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבא's Step 2 answer after Steps 3–4 showed it does not fit רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replacement answer that changes the reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: עדים זוממין are exempt because voice is not an action.
steps.terutzMaskana: עדים זוממין are exempt because their testimony is based on sight, which is not an action. This works even for רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: Defining a necromancer and a sorcerer
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא defines a בעל אוב and a ידעוני.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: a בעל אוב is one who makes the dead speak from between his joints and from his armpits. A ידעוני is one who puts the bone of a ידוע in his mouth, and the bone speaks by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic by quoting a ברייתא that defines two kinds of forbidden sorcery. This sets up the challenges that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא tells us exactly what each one does. With a בעל אוב, the voice of the dead comes from the sorcerer's joints or armpits. With a ידעוני, a bone placed in the mouth speaks on its own. The detail that the voice comes from the joints is what the next steps will challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Necromancer, one who raises the dead to speak.
A type of sorcerer who uses the bone of a ידוע.
Joints of the body.
His armpits.
The name of a certain animal whose bone is used.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A necromancer:
this is one who speaks from between the joints
phrases.notes: He means the voice of the dead is heard coming out of the sorcerer's joints.

phrases.english: and from between his armpits.
A sorcerer [yideoni]:
this is one who places a bone of a yadua in his mouth,
and it speaks on its own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the side discussion about עדים זוממין to define the בעל אוב and ידעוני themselves.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בעל אוב makes the dead speak from his joints or armpits. A ידעוני uses a bone in his mouth that speaks by itself.

steps.title: A verse suggests the dead speaks normally
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא from a פסוק in ישעיהו that describes a voice coming from the ground like an אוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: the פסוק says, "Your voice shall be like an אוב from the ground." Doesn't this mean the dead speaks in his normal way?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק that seems to clash with the ברייתא's definition of a בעל אוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the voice comes from between the sorcerer's joints. The פסוק describes the voice coming from the ground. That makes it sound like the dead speaks the normal way, from its own place, and not from the joints.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not that? This introduces the reading behind the challenge.
In his normal way.
Speaks.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
"And your voice shall be as a ghost out of the ground."
Is it not that he speaks in his normal way?
phrases.notes: The dead seems to speak from the ground, and not from the sorcerer's joints.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the definition of בעל אוב given in Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that a בעל אוב's voice comes from between the joints.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק says the voice comes from the ground, which suggests the dead speaks normally and not from the joints.

steps.title: The dead rises and speaks from the joints
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the dead rises up, sits between the sorcerer's joints, and speaks from there.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The dead rises up, sits between the joints, and speaks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge and shows that the פסוק and the ברייתא fit together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "From the ground" describes where the dead comes up from. The actual speaking still happens from between the sorcerer's joints, exactly as the ברייתא said.

keyTerms.meaning: Rises up.
Sits.

phrases.english: No, he rises and sits
between the joints and speaks.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, דְּסָלֵיק וְיָתֵיב בֵּין הַפְּרָקִים וּמִשְׁתַּעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dead speaks normally, from the ground.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dead comes up from the ground but speaks from between the sorcerer's joints.

steps.title: Saul's story suggests the dead speaks normally
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries again with the story of the woman and שאול, where she saw a being coming up out of the earth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: "The woman said to שאול, I see a godlike being coming up out of the earth." Doesn't this mean the dead speaks in his normal way?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second פסוק that seems to show the dead speaking on its own, not from the joints.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this story the woman sees the dead rising, and he then speaks with שאול. That sounds like normal speech, which again seems to go against the ברייתא's definition.

keyTerms.meaning: King שאול, who consulted a בעלת אוב.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"And the woman said to Saul,
I see a godlike being coming up out of the earth."
Is it not that he spoke in his normal way?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge against the definition in Step 6, in the same pattern as Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that the voice comes from between the joints.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the story of שאול, the dead seems to rise and speak on its own.

steps.title: Again, the dead speaks from the joints
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: here too the dead sits between the joints and speaks.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. He sits between the joints and speaks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the second challenge with the same answer it gave before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even in the story of שאול, the dead may well have spoken from between the woman's joints. So the פסוק does not prove that the dead speaks normally, and the ברייתא's definition stands.
steps.whatToRemember: With a בעל אוב, the dead comes up, but its voice is heard from between the sorcerer's joints. Both פסוקים fit this.

phrases.english: No, he sits
between the joints and speaks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 9 with the same answer as Step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the story of שאול.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק can be read as the dead speaking from between the joints, so it proves nothing.

steps.title: Two kinds of necromancer and how they differ
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a בעל אוב can raise the dead with his זכור or ask questions of a skull. The first does not work in the normal way or on שבת. The second works in the normal way and even on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: a בעל אוב is either one who raises the dead with his זכור, or one who asks questions of a skull. What is the difference? With the זכור, the dead does not come up in its normal way and does not come up on שבת. With the skull, the dead comes up in its normal way and even on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that splits בעל אוב into two types and lists two differences between them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both methods count as בעל אוב, but they work differently. The זכור method fails on שבת and does not bring the dead up the normal way. The skull method works the normal way and even on שבת. This שבת detail sets up the story that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: his זכור, a body part used in this kind of sorcery
a skull
in its normal way
what is the difference between this and that?

phrases.english: The Sages taught: a בעל אוב is
both one who raises the dead with his זכור,
and one who asks questions of a skull.
What is the difference between this one and that one?
One who raises with his זכור: the dead does not come up in its normal way,
phrases.notes: 'Not in its normal way' means the dead appears upside down.

phrases.english: and it does not come up on שבת.
One who asks of a skull: the dead comes up in its normal way,
and it comes up even on שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new ברייתא that breaks the category of בעל אוב into two methods.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בעל אוב is either the זכור type or the skull type. The זכור type does not work in the normal way or on שבת. The skull type works in the normal way and even on שבת.

steps.title: How can a skull 'rise' if it is already there?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the word 'rises' for the skull method, since the skull is already lying in front of the sorcerer.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Rises'? Where does it rise to? The skull is lying right in front of him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks one word in the ברייתא. A skull that is already sitting there cannot 'rise.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'rises' fits the זכור method, where the dead comes up from the ground. With a skull nothing comes up, because the skull is already present. So the wording seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: where does it go up to?
it is lying in front of him

phrases.english: 'Rises'? Where does it rise to?
It is lying right in front of him!

steps.triggerLanguage: עוֹלֶה? לְהֵיכָא סָלֵיק? הָא קַמֵּיהּ מַנַּח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ברייתא's last clause.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word 'עולה' in the skull clause of the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Something already lying in front of you cannot 'rise,' so the word does not fit the skull method.

steps.title: Read it as 'answers,' not 'rises'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the wording: with the skull, the dead answers in its normal way and answers even on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: it answers in its normal way, and it answers even on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the ברייתא's wording by swapping 'rises' (עולה) for 'answers' (עונה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The skull does not go anywhere. It only gives answers. So the ברייתא should be read as saying the skull answers normally, even on שבת. The difference between the two methods stays the same; only the word changes.

keyTerms.meaning: rather, say (a correction of the wording)
answers

phrases.english: Rather, say:
it answers in its normal way, and it answers even on שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge by correcting the text.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means the skull 'answers' normally, even on שבת.

steps.title: טורנוסרופוס asks what makes שבת different
steps.stepSummary: Linking to the idea that the dead do not come up on שבת, the גמרא tells how טורנוסרופוס asked רבי עקיבא what makes this day different from other days.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wicked טורנוסרופוס also asked רבי עקיבא this question. He said to him: What makes this day different from other days?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story. טורנוסרופוס challenges רבי עקיבא about why שבת should be special at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said the dead do not come up on שבת, which suggests שבת has real power in the world. טורנוסרופוס questions this: one day is like any other. This opens a back-and-forth.

keyTerms.meaning: the wicked טורנוסרופוס, a Roman governor
a day, compared to other days

phrases.english: And this question was also asked
by the wicked טורנוסרופוס, of רבי עקיבא.
He said to him: And what makes this day different from other days?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף שְׁאֵלָה זוֹ שָׁאַל טוֹרָנוּסְרוּפוּס הָרָשָׁע אֶת רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא's point about שבת to bring a related story.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What makes שבת different from any other day?

steps.title: שבת is special because my Master wants it
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא answers with his own question: what makes you more important than other men? When טורנוסרופוס says 'my master (the emperor) wants it,' רבי עקיבא replies that שבת too is special because his Master, ה׳, wants it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to him: And what makes this man more important than other men? He answered: Because my master wants it. רבי עקיבא said: שבת too is special because my Master wants it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא answers by comparing שבת to טורנוסרופוס's own high rank.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טורנוסרופוס is not more important by nature. He is important because the emperor chose him. In the same way, שבת is special because ה׳ chose it. Being chosen by the master, not some natural difference, is what makes something special.

keyTerms.meaning: a man, compared to other men
because my master wants it

phrases.english: He said to him: And what makes this man more important than other men?
He said to him: Because my master wants it.
phrases.notes: His 'master' here is the Roman emperor, who gave him his rank.

phrases.english: שבת too is special because my Master wants it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers טורנוסרופוס's question by comparison.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שבת is special because ה׳ chose it, just as טורנוסרופוס is important because the emperor chose him.

steps.title: How do you know today is really שבת?
steps.stepSummary: טורנוסרופוס changes his question: even if שבת is special, how do you know that today is the real שבת?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what I meant to ask you: Who says that today is שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: טורנוסרופוס changes his question. Now he asks how anyone can know which day is the true שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He accepts that ה׳ could make a day special. But maybe the count of days got mixed up, and the real שבת is a different day. So now he wants proof that this day is the one.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what I meant to say to you
who is to say?
now, today

phrases.english: He said to him: This is what I meant to say to you:
Who says that today is שבת?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי קָאָמֵינָא לָךְ: מִי יֵימַר דְּהָאִידָּנָא שַׁבְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Changes the question after רבי עקיבא's first answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can we know which day is the real שבת?

steps.title: Three signs that prove which day is שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא brings three proofs: the סבטיון River, the בעל אוב, and the grave of טורנוסרופוס's father, which does not give off smoke on שבת. טורנוסרופוס answers that רבי עקיבא has shamed and cursed his father.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The סבטיון River will prove it, a בעל אוב will prove it, and your father's grave will prove it, because it does not give off smoke on שבת. He said to him: You have disgraced him, shamed him, and cursed him!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives three signs from the world that show which day is שבת. The last one stings טורנוסרופוס personally.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each sign behaves differently on שבת, so it marks the real day. The בעל אוב sign ties back to the ברייתא: the dead do not come up on שבת. The father's grave sign suggests that his father is being punished all week but rests on שבת, which is why טורנוסרופוס feels his father was cursed.

keyTerms.meaning: the סבטיון River, which rests on שבת
will prove it
smoke
you disgraced him, shamed him, and cursed him

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's rule that the dead do not come up on שבת becomes one of רבי עקיבא's proofs that we know which day is the true שבת.

phrases.english: He said to him: The סבטיון River will prove it,
phrases.notes: This river is calm only on שבת.

phrases.english: a בעל אוב will prove it,
his father's grave will prove it,
because it does not give off smoke on שבת.
He said to him: You have disgraced him, shamed him, and cursed him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of how we know which day is שבת.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Three signs that act differently on שבת (the river, the בעל אוב, and the father's grave) show which day is the true שבת.

steps.title: Aren't שואל אוב and דורש אל המתים the same?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that שואל אוב seems to be the same as דורש אל המתים, so why does the פסוק list them separately?
steps.simpleTranslation: One who asks a necromancer: isn't that exactly what the פסוק calls "one who inquires of the dead"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the פסוק seems to say the same thing twice. It asks why שואל אוב and דורש אל המתים are listed as two separate items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בעל אוב brings up the dead to answer questions, and that already sounds like "inquiring of the dead." If the two are the same, the second phrase in the פסוק adds nothing. So the גמרא challenges us to find a different meaning for דורש אל המתים.

keyTerms.meaning: One who asks a necromancer (a בעל אוב) to bring up the dead
One who seeks information from the dead
That is the same as (a word the גמרא uses to point out repetition)

phrases.english: One who asks a necromancer,
that is the same as "or one who inquires of the dead"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic after the story of טורנוסרופוס, going back to the list in the פסוק
steps.kashyaTarget: The פסוק listing both שואל אוב and דורש אל המתים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Redundancy: the two phrases seem to describe the same practice, so one of them looks extra

steps.title: דורש אל המתים is sleeping in a graveyard
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that דורש אל המתים is a different practice: starving oneself and sleeping in a graveyard to get a רוח טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who inquires of the dead is explained in a ברייתא: he starves himself and goes to sleep in a graveyard so that a spirit of impurity will rest on him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by bringing a ברייתא. It shows that דורש אל המתים means a different method of reaching the dead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בעל אוב brings up a specific dead person. A דורש אל המתים does not bring anyone up. He prepares himself by fasting and sleeping among graves so that a רוח טומאה rests on him. Because the methods are different, the פסוק needs to list both.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
One who starves himself
Graveyard
A spirit of impurity

phrases.english: One who inquires of the dead,
is as it is taught:
"or one who inquires of the dead":
this is one who starves himself
and goes and spends the night in a graveyard,
so that a spirit of impurity will rest upon him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the redundancy question by defining דורש אל המתים as a separate practice
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: two different methods
steps.terutzHavaAmina: דורש אל המתים is just another name for שואל אוב
steps.terutzMaskana: דורש אל המתים is fasting and sleeping in a graveyard to receive a רוח טומאה, which is a separate practice
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא sets up the image that רבי עקיבא builds on in the next step.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא cries over the power of impurity and purity
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא reasons with a קל וחומר: if starving for impurity works, starving for purity should work even more. But our sins separate us from ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי עקיבא reached this פסוק he would cry. He said: if someone starves himself to get a spirit of impurity, and it really comes, then someone who starves himself to get a spirit of purity should surely get it. But what can I do? Our sins cause it, as the פסוק says, "your sins have separated between you and your God."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an aggadic teaching connected to the ברייתא. רבי עקיבא would cry when he learned this פסוק, and he explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא builds a קל וחומר‎: ה׳'s power to give purity is greater than the power of impurity, so effort toward purity should succeed even more. Yet in practice we do not receive a רוח טהרה. He blames our sins and proves it from a פסוק in ישעיהו.

keyTerms.meaning: A פסוק (verse)
A spirit of purity and holiness
How much more so (the ending of a קל וחומר)
Our sins
Separate, divide

steps.confusionAlert: רבי עקיבא is not saying the method of the דורש אל המתים is good. He is saying that if even impurity answers effort, holiness should answer effort even more, and only sin stands in the way.

phrases.aramaic: וּכְשֶׁהָיָה רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מַגִּיעַ לְמִקְרָא זֶה
phrases.english: And when Rabbi Akiva would reach this verse
he would cry,
and he said: if one who starves himself
so that a spirit of impurity will rest upon him
does have a spirit of impurity rest upon him,
then one who starves himself
so that a spirit of purity will rest upon him
how much more so should it rest on him!
But what can I do,
for our sins have caused this for us,
as it is stated:
"But your sins have separated
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 59:2. The word in square brackets is the corrected wording, so it matches the פסוק.

phrases.english: between you and your God."

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְשֶׁהָיָה רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מַגִּיעַ לְמִקְרָא זֶה הָיָה בּוֹכֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds an aggadic lesson on the ברייתא's description of the one who starves himself
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Effort toward purity should succeed even more than effort toward impurity; only our sins block it

steps.title: רבא: righteous people could create a world
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns from the same פסוק that if צדיקים were free of sin, they could create a world.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: if the righteous wanted to, they could create a world, as it says, "your sins have separated between you and your God."
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds his own lesson from the same פסוק רבי עקיבא used. The next two steps bring stories that back up his claim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says only sins separate a person from ה׳. So a צדיק with no sins would have no separation, and could do what ה׳ does, even create a world. רבא takes רבי עקיבא's idea one step further.

keyTerms.meaning: If they wanted
Righteous people
They could create a world

steps.whatToRemember: דורש אל המתים is a separate practice from שואל אוב. From it, רבי עקיבא and רבא learn that only sin keeps us from holiness, and that a sinless צדיק has enormous power.

phrases.english: Rava said:
If the righteous wanted,
they could create a world,
as it is stated:
"But your sins have separated, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אִי בָּעוּ צַדִּיקֵי, בָּרוּ עָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same פסוק as רבי עקיבא to teach a further lesson about the power of צדיקים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sinless צדיקים have no separation from ה׳ and could even create a world

steps.title: רבא creates a man who cannot speak
steps.stepSummary: רבא created a man and sent him to רבי זירא. The man could not answer, so רבי זירא realized a Sage made him and told him to return to dust.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא created a man and sent him to רבי זירא. רבי זירא spoke to him, but the man did not answer. רבי זירא said: You were made by one of the Sages. Go back to your dust.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that backs up רבא's statement from the last step, that צדיקים can create.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא really did create a man, which shows that צדיקים have real power to create. But the man could not speak, and that is how רבי זירא could tell he was not a natural person but a creation of one of the Sages.

keyTerms.meaning: A man (here, a man created by רבא)
He sent him
The group of Sages
Dust

steps.confusionAlert: This story does not say רבא did something forbidden. He created the man with holy powers. Do not mix it up with the כישוף this סוגיא discusses elsewhere.

phrases.english: Rava created a man.
He sent him before Rabbi Zeira.
Rabbi Zeira was speaking with him,
but he would not answer him.
He said to him: You are from the members of the group,
phrases.notes: He means one of the Sages made you, and that's why you can't talk.

phrases.english: Return to your dust.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-life example backing up רבא's statement in step 21.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that צדיקים could create a world if they had no sin
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבא creating a man and sending him to רבי זירא

steps.title: Two Sages create a calf every Friday
steps.stepSummary: רב חנינא and רב אושעיא learned ספר יצירה every ערב שבת, created a calf, and ate it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנינא and רב אושעיא would sit every ערב שבת and learn ספר יצירה. A third-born calf would be created for them, and they would eat it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second story showing that צדיקים can create.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story goes a step further than the one before. The calf was a full, real animal, good enough to eat. So it shows the power of צדיקים to create through holiness, using ספר יצירה.

keyTerms.meaning: ערב שבת, Friday
The Book of Creation, a holy work about how the world was created
A third-born calf (an especially good calf)

steps.whatToRemember: Both stories support רבא: צדיקים truly can create through holiness. Still, רבא's man could not speak, and that is how רבי זירא knew a Sage had made him.

phrases.english: Rav Chanina and Rav Oshaya
would sit every Shabbat eve,
and engage in Sefer Yetzirah,
and a third-born calf would be created for them,
and they would eat it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חֲנִינָא וְרַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא הֲווֹ יָתְבִי כׇּל מַעֲלֵי שַׁבְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, stronger example supporting the same point as step 22.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that צדיקים can create
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רב חנינא and רב אושעיא creating a calf with ספר יצירה

steps.title: Three definitions of a soothsayer
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives three opinions on what a מעונן is: רבי שמעון, the חכמים, and רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: What is a מעונן? רבי שמעון says: someone who passes seven kinds of זכור over the eye. The חכמים say: someone who tricks people's eyes. רבי עקיבא says: someone who figures out lucky times and hours, and says 'Today is a good day to travel,' 'Tomorrow is a good day to buy,' 'In the years before שמיטה the wheat is usually good,' 'Pulling up beans by the roots keeps them from going bad.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: what exactly the forbidden practice of מעונן is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three opinions. רבי שמעון says it is a real magic act done on the eye. The חכמים say it is fake magic that tricks people's eyes. רבי עקיבא says it is someone who claims to know which times are lucky, even with no act at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A soothsayer, a forbidden practice in the תורה
A kind of seed used in this practice
One who tricks the eyes, like a sleight-of-hand trick
Times and hours (which ones are 'lucky')
שמיטה years

steps.whyThisMatters: According to רבי עקיבא, even just picking 'lucky days' to act on counts as the forbidden practice of מעונן.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: 'A soothsayer' —
Rabbi Shimon says:

phrases.aramaic: זֶה הַמַּעֲבִיר שִׁבְעָה מִינֵי זְכוּר עַל הָעַיִן.
phrases.english: This is one who passes seven kinds of zechur over the eye.

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: זֶה הָאוֹחֵז אֶת הָעֵינַיִם.
phrases.english: And the Sages say: This is one who tricks the eyes.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: זֶה הַמְחַשֵּׁב עִתִּים וְשָׁעוֹת
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: This is one who calculates times and hours
and says: 'Today is good for setting out,'
'Tomorrow is good for buying,'
'Usually, in the years before the Sabbatical Year, the wheat is good,'
'Uprooting legumes keeps them from going bad.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the stories about creating and starts defining the forbidden practices in the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a מחלוקת over what a מעונן is: a real magic act on the eye (רבי שמעון), tricking the eyes (חכמים), or claiming certain times are lucky (רבי עקיבא).

steps.title: What a diviner looks like
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא defines a מנחש as someone who treats everyday events as signs, like dropping his bread or seeing an animal on the road.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A מנחש is one who says: 'His bread fell from his mouth,' 'His stick fell from his hand,' 'His son called him from behind,' 'A raven called to him,' 'A deer blocked his way,' 'A snake on his right,' and 'A fox on his left.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא, this time defining the forbidden practice of מנחש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מנחש takes ordinary events and treats them as bad signs about what will happen. The ברייתא gives a list of examples so we can recognize this kind of superstition.

keyTerms.meaning: A diviner, one who reads signs from random events
His stick
A raven
Blocked him, cut across his path

steps.whatToRemember: A מעונן is about 'lucky times' (according to רבי עקיבא). A מנחש is about reading signs from random events. Both are forbidden by the same פסוק.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: 'An enchanter' — this is one who says:
'His bread fell from his mouth,'
'His staff fell from his hand,'
'His son calls him from behind,'
'A raven calls to him,'
'A deer blocked him on the road,'
'A snake is on his right,' and 'A fox is on his left.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues defining the forbidden practices in the פסוק, moving from מעונן to מנחש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מנחש is someone who treats random events (dropped bread, animals on the road, a child calling him) as signs about what will happen.
